generator: extracted from cachekit-rs v0.5.1 + cachekit-ts v0.1.0 (Python ground truth); arrow/orjson/original_type and standard_serializer vectors generated with cryptography/OpenSSL (fixed nonces) matching real cachekit-py serializer metadata (the standard_serializer plaintexts are cachekit-py 0.22.0's own: python-frame.json's default and integrity-off payloads), verified by tools/encryption-verify.py; master_key_input rows hand-written from one key, the sealed rows sealed with the stdlib HKDF + cryptography AES-GCM (fixed nonce)

configuration.note: spec/encryption.md § Key Rotation (Keyring). Configurations a keyring is loaded from: a current master key and a list of decrypt-only master keys, as CACHEKIT_MASTER_KEY and CACHEKIT_PREVIOUS_MASTER_KEYS (comma-separated) or an SDK's own parameters give them. A conforming SDK accepts each accept row and refuses each reject row when the keyring is loaded, before any entry is read. No row's verdict depends on what the spec leaves open: uppercase hex (intent-presets.md § Master Key Input rule 1) or a key repeated within the decrypt-only list. Each note names mistakes its row catches; tools/encryption-verify.py checks that each one misjudges its row.

vectors.name: keyring_three_decrypt_only_keys
vectors.note: One current key and three decrypt-only keys, the cap, each a valid 32-byte key and none repeated. A conforming SDK accepts it at load. One whose cap is below three refuses it.

vectors.name: keyring_four_decrypt_only_keys
vectors.note: One current key and four decrypt-only keys, one over the cap, each a valid 32-byte key and none repeated, so nothing but the count can refuse it. A conforming SDK refuses it at load. One with no cap accepts it, and so does one that keeps the first three keys and drops the rest.

vectors.name: keyring_current_key_decrypt_only
vectors.note: The current key repeated, as given, between two other decrypt-only keys. A conforming SDK refuses it at load. One that does not compare the current key with the decrypt-only keys accepts it, and so does one that compares it only with the first or only with the last.

vectors.name: keyring_current_key_decrypt_only_uppercase
vectors.note: The current key repeated in the decrypt-only list in uppercase hex. Its verdict does not depend on uppercase handling, which spec/intent-presets.md § Master Key Input rule 1 leaves open: an SDK that refuses uppercase hex refuses the list, and one that reads it as the same bytes finds the repeat. One that accepts uppercase hex and compares the keys as strings accepts it, and so does one that accepts uppercase hex and does not compare the current key with the decrypt-only keys.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_compressed_false_sealed_true
aad_reject_vectors.note: compressed_basic's ciphertext, sealed with compressed True, presented with compressed False, as a reader configured without compression builds it. A reader that retries with the other compressed value decrypts it, to deadbeefcafe, which no container reads, so the retry still ends with no value and only a test that asserts the authentication failure itself tells it apart.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_compressed_true_sealed_false
aad_reject_vectors.note: basic_bytes's ciphertext, sealed with compressed False, presented with compressed True, as a reader configured with compression builds it. A reader that retries with the other compressed value, as one that falls back to compressed False for entries it takes for legacy ones does, decrypts it, to bytes that are no ByteStorage envelope, so the envelope reader still ends with no value and only a test that asserts the authentication failure itself tells the retry apart.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_format_msgpack_sealed_arrow
aad_reject_vectors.note: arrow_uncompressed's ciphertext, sealed with the format token arrow, presented with msgpack and the same original_type, as cachekit-py builds it from a frame header claiming msgpack. A reader that retries with the other registry format tokens, an Arrow reader's own arrow among them, decrypts it, to eight bytes that hold no Arrow IPC file, so the Arrow reader still ends with no value and only a test that asserts the authentication failure itself tells the retry apart.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_without_original_type_sealed_with
aad_reject_vectors.note: original_type_numpy's ciphertext, sealed with the fifth component original_type numpy, presented with four components, as a reader that never adds original_type (cachekit-ts, cachekit-rs, interop mode) or a cachekit-py frame header without one presents it. A reader that retries with each original_type value cachekit-py emits decrypts it, to [1, 2, 3], one MessagePack document, which the plain-MessagePack reader that presents this AAD returns as a value.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_with_original_type_sealed_without
aad_reject_vectors.note: basic_bytes's ciphertext, sealed with four components, presented with the fifth component original_type msgpack, as cachekit-py's StandardSerializer with integrity checking off builds it. A reader that retries without original_type after a five-component attempt fails, to read entries cachekit-ts, cachekit-rs or interop mode wrote, decrypts it, to 01 and seven more bytes: one MessagePack document with bytes after it. A plain-MessagePack reader that refuses those bytes still ends with no value, and one that ignores them returns 1. Only an interop reader must refuse them (spec/interop-mode.md), so a test tells a retry apart only by asserting the authentication failure itself.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_key_with_prefix_sealed_without
aad_reject_vectors.note: basic_bytes's ciphertext, sealed under the cache_key test:vector:1, presented under app:test:vector:1, the key with a prefix in front. A reader whose cache_key carries a namespace or key prefix and that retries with the key stripped of it decrypts it, to 01 and seven more bytes: one MessagePack document with bytes after it. A plain-MessagePack reader that refuses those bytes still ends with no value, and one that ignores them returns 1. Only an interop reader must refuse them (spec/interop-mode.md), so a test tells a retry apart only by asserting the authentication failure itself.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_compressed_false_sealed_true_five_components
aad_reject_vectors.note: standard_serializer_default's ciphertext, cachekit-py's default AAD shape sealed with compressed True, presented with compressed False, as cachekit-py's StandardSerializer with integrity checking off builds it. A reader that retries with the other compressed value, or flips the flag only on five-component AADs, the shape of every cachekit-py entry, decrypts it, to a ByteStorage envelope, one MessagePack document, whose 4-element array the plain-MessagePack reader that presents this AAD may return as a value; one that also takes its container from the flag unwraps it to the value.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_compressed_true_sealed_false_five_components
aad_reject_vectors.note: standard_serializer_integrity_off's ciphertext, sealed with compressed False and five components, presented with compressed True, as cachekit-py's StandardSerializer with integrity checking on builds it. A reader that retries with the other compressed value, or flips the flag only on five-component AADs, decrypts it, to plain MessagePack, which the envelope reader that presents this AAD still reads as no value, so only a test that asserts the authentication failure itself tells the retry apart, unless that reader also takes its container from the flag and returns the map.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_without_original_type_sealed_with_msgpack
aad_reject_vectors.note: standard_serializer_default's ciphertext, sealed with the fifth component original_type msgpack, presented with four components, as a reader configured for a ByteStorage envelope that never adds original_type (cachekit-ts with compression on) builds it. A reader that retries with each original_type value cachekit-py emits, or only with msgpack, its own serializer's, decrypts it, to the envelope, which that reader unwraps to the value.

aad_reject_vectors.name: aad_format_arrow_sealed_msgpack
aad_reject_vectors.note: standard_serializer_default's ciphertext, sealed with the format token msgpack, presented with arrow and the same compressed value and original_type, as cachekit-py builds it from a frame header claiming arrow. A reader that retries with the other registry format tokens, or only with msgpack, its own serializer's, decrypts it, to the envelope, which a StandardSerializer reader unwraps to the value.

decrypted_container.note: spec/encryption.md § AAD v0x03 Format, ENC-2 and ENC-3: after decryption the container is the one the reader is configured for, never one picked by looking at the bytes or tried after another fails, and a parse mismatch hard-fails. Each row is sealed under the main master key and tenant_id with the AAD of the reader it names: plain_msgpack (four components, compressed False; cachekit-ts with compression off, cachekit-rs, interop mode), interop (the same AAD under one of interop-mode.json's keys, for interop mode's reader, which MUST consume exactly one document), bytestorage_envelope (four components, compressed True; cachekit-ts with compression on), arrow_checksummed (format and original_type arrow, compressed False over uncompressed IPC; cachekit-py's ArrowSerializer) or orjson_checksummed (format and original_type orjson, compressed False; cachekit-py's OrjsonSerializer with integrity checking on). Its plaintext is a container that reader is not configured for, or one it must not unwrap. outcome is what a conforming read returns: error, no value (an error, or a miss under the SDK's fail-open policy), or not_unwrapped, anything but the value inside the plaintext's container: the plaintext decoded as one MessagePack document, or no value. Each note names mistakes its row catches; tools/encryption-verify.py checks that each one returns a value its row's outcome forbids.

vectors.name: container_envelope_to_plain_reader
vectors.note: A valid ByteStorage envelope, python-frame.json's default write payload, whose inner value is the map {user_id: 42, name: cachekit, active: true}, sealed under the AAD a plain-MessagePack reader builds. The reader must not return the map inside it: it decodes the plaintext as one MessagePack document, the envelope's 4-element array, or returns no value. A reader that unwraps a plaintext which parses as an envelope returns the map.

vectors.name: container_trailing_byte_to_interop_reader
vectors.note: interop-mode.json's issue_example_object value followed by one 00 byte, the input of its reader_trailing_byte reject vector, sealed under the AAD an interop reader builds for interop-mode.json's bool_null key. An interop reader MUST consume exactly one document (spec/interop-mode.md), after a decrypt as before one, so the read returns no value. A reader that ignores bytes after the first document, as one that checks for them only on plaintext entries does after a decrypt, returns the value, and so does one that strips trailing NUL bytes before a strict decode.

vectors.name: container_plain_to_envelope_reader
vectors.note: The same map's plain MessagePack, sealed under the AAD an envelope reader builds. It is not a ByteStorage envelope, so the read returns no value. A reader that falls back to plain MessagePack when the envelope does not parse returns the map.

vectors.name: container_bare_arrow_to_arrow_reader
vectors.note: python-frame.json's arrow_compression_off_write payload without its 8-byte xxHash3-64 checksum: a bare Arrow IPC file, sealed under the AAD cachekit-py's ArrowSerializer builds for that write. The arrow container is [checksum][Arrow IPC file], so the read returns no value. A reader that accepts Arrow IPC with no checksum prefix returns the table.

vectors.name: container_plain_json_to_orjson_reader
vectors.note: python-frame.json's forged_plaintext_orjson payload without its 8-byte xxHash3-64 checksum: plain JSON, sealed under the AAD cachekit-py's OrjsonSerializer builds. A reader with integrity checking on reads [checksum][JSON], so the read returns no value. A reader that falls back to plain JSON when the checksum layout does not parse returns the map.

vectors.name: container_incomplete_tail_to_interop_reader
vectors.note: The same value followed by 91, the header of a one-element array with no element: an incomplete second document, sealed under the AAD an interop reader builds for interop-mode.json's issue_example_mixed key. An interop reader returns no value. One that ignores bytes after the first document returns the value, and so does one that refuses only a second complete document, as container_trailing_byte_to_interop_reader's 00 is.

default_tenant.note: spec/intent-presets.md § Master Key Input rule 5: with no caller-supplied tenant every SDK MUST derive keys and build AAD with the literal "default". Same master key as the main set; sealed with the stdlib HKDF + cryptography AES-GCM reference (fixed nonce), verified by tools/encryption-verify.py. The cache_key is interop-mode.json key_vectors[single_int].expected_key and the plaintext is value_vectors[issue_example_object] — the vector is directly loadable as an interop-mode entry.

master_key_input.note: spec/intent-presets.md § Master Key Input. Rules 1 and 3: the secure preset takes the master key as a hex string, derives the key bytes as hex_decode(string), the same in every SDK, accepts 32 bytes and refuses fewer. Rule 4: an entry point that takes raw key bytes takes exactly 32. Every row comes from one key, master_key_every_hex_digit's, which is the accept row the other notes name: master_key_first_byte_80 is that key with its first byte, 00, replaced by 80, and each reject row cuts or alters it. A conforming SDK passes every row (they are necessary, not sufficient): a hex entry point given an accept row's master_key_hex and no tenant derives the pinned fingerprint and decrypts the sealed entry, every hex entry point refuses each reject row's master_key_hex, and every raw-bytes entry point refuses each raw reject row's bytes (raw_key_hex decoded). The accept rows are lowercase hex, which is what openssl rand -hex 32, the key generator encryption.md gives, prints. Rule 1 does not say whether a key may hold uppercase letters, white space or a 0x prefix, so no row's verdict depends on it: a row that holds white space or a 0x prefix is refused whether a decoder drops those characters or refuses them. Each row also gets the same verdict whether an SDK accepts exactly 32 bytes or 32 and more, as rule 3 allows either. Each note names mistakes its row catches. Sealed with the stdlib HKDF and cryptography's AES-GCM (fixed nonce); verified by tools/encryption-verify.py, which also checks that each mistake a note names misjudges its row.

accept_vectors.name: master_key_every_hex_digit
accept_vectors.note: 32 distinct bytes: a leading 00 byte, 14 bytes above 7f, and every hex digit, in lowercase, in both places of a byte. A decoder that reverses the bytes, swaps the two digits of each byte or misreads a letter derives another key: its fingerprint differs and the entry does not decrypt. One that passes the bytes through a text string (a str-typed boundary, where each byte above 7f becomes two) reads 46 bytes, so it refuses the key or derives another. A validator that admits only digits or only uppercase letters, a table for a byte's first digit that holds only 0-9, or a signed-byte parser that refuses a pair above 7f refuses the key; so does a big-integer decoder, unsigned or two's complement (BigInteger.toByteArray(), to_signed_bytes_be), whose bytes are checked for 32 without padding: it drops the leading 00 byte, and byte 1 is below 80, so no sign byte restores it. Fed as raw bytes, it catches a raw-bytes entry point that passes them through a text string. The entry is interop-mode.json's empty_args key holding its mixed_array value, sealed under this key and the tenant "default". It shares neither cache_key nor plaintext with default_tenant_interop, so a test can plant both in one backend and tell them apart, as reading with one key current and the other previous needs.

accept_vectors.name: master_key_first_byte_80
accept_vectors.note: The accept row's key with its first byte, 00, replaced by 80, so the key's top bit is set. A two's-complement big-integer decoder padded to 32 bytes reads every key whose first byte is below 80 correctly, the accept row's included, but this key needs a 33rd byte for its sign: Python's int(key, 16).to_bytes(32, "big", signed=True) behind a strict hex check refuses it, and Java's BigInteger.toByteArray() left-padded to 32 bytes behind a 64-character check returns 33 bytes, which a check that the key is exactly 32 bytes refuses and a check for 32 bytes or more reads as another key. The entry is interop-mode.json's uuid_lowercased key holding its float_value_stays_float64 value, sealed under this key and the tenant "default". It shares neither cache_key nor plaintext with the accept row or default_tenant_interop, so a test can plant all three in one backend and tell them apart.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_odd_65_digits
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's 64 digits followed by 0: 65 characters, so not hex. A decoder that drops the odd last digit, as Node's Buffer.from does, reads the accept row's key, so it accepts the string unless it checks for an odd length. An entry point that requires exactly 64 characters refuses it for its length.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_odd_63_digits
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's first 63 digits, so not hex. A decoder that pads an odd string with a leading 0 reads 32 bytes, so it accepts the string even behind a check that the key is exactly 32 bytes. An entry point that requires exactly 64 characters refuses it for its length.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_non_hex_digit
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's 64 digits with the last replaced by g. A decoder that reads a character that is not a hex digit as 0 accepts it as 32 bytes. One that stops at that character, as Node's Buffer.from does, keeps the 31 bytes before it, and accepts them when only the string's length is checked, including behind a pattern anchored only at the start (re.match, or /^[0-9a-f]+/ without $): the g comes last, so such a pattern passes it.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_trailing_non_hex
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's 64 digits followed by gg: 66 characters, an even length. A decoder that stops at the first pair that is not hex, as Node's Buffer.from does, reads the accept row's key and accepts it behind either length rule, even after a check that the length is even, which the 65-digit row cannot show: the shape of Buffer.from(key, "hex") followed by key.length === 32.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_plus_sign
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's 64 digits with the leading 0 replaced by +, so the first pair is +0. An integer parser that takes a sign reads +0 as 0, so one used pair by pair (Rust's u8::from_str_radix, Python's int(pair, 16)), or on the whole string (int(key, 16) back to 32 bytes), reads the accept row's key behind a 64-character check.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_31_bytes
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's first 31 bytes (62 characters). An entry point with no length check, one that accepts 31 bytes (off by one) or 16 (the HKDF floor encryption.md once listed as the minimum), or one that pads a short key to 32 bytes accepts it.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_24_bytes
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's first 24 bytes (48 characters). Besides the mistakes the 31-byte row catches, other than off by one, a validator that admits AES-192 and AES-256 key sizes (24 or 32 bytes), with or without 16, accepts it.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_16_bytes
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's first 16 bytes (32 characters). Besides the mistakes the 31-byte row catches, other than off by one, a validator that admits AES-128 and AES-256 key sizes (16 or 32 bytes) accepts it while refusing 24 and 31 bytes.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_31_bytes_and_crlf
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's first 31 bytes followed by CR LF: 64 characters. Whether a decoder drops white space or refuses it, the key is short or malformed, so every reading of rule 1 refuses it. An entry point that checks for 64 characters on the string as given, then trims it and decodes strictly with no check on the key's length, accepts a 31-byte key.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_31_bytes_with_spaces
reject_vectors.note: The accept row's first 31 bytes with a space after the first byte and another after the second: 64 characters. Whether a decoder drops white space or refuses it, the key is short or malformed, so every reading of rule 1 refuses it. An entry point that strips white space from the ends, checks for 64 characters, then decodes with Python's bytes.fromhex, which skips the spaces between pairs, accepts a 31-byte key.

reject_vectors.name: master_key_0x_and_31_bytes
reject_vectors.note: 0x followed by the accept row's first 31 bytes: 64 characters. Whether a decoder strips a 0x prefix or refuses it, the key is short or malformed, so every reading of rule 1 refuses it. An entry point that checks for 64 characters, then strips a 0x prefix and decodes what is left, accepts a 31-byte key.

raw_reject_vectors.name: raw_key_31_bytes
raw_reject_vectors.note: Raw key bytes: the accept row's first 31 bytes, written in hex only because JSON holds no bytes. A raw-bytes entry point that admits 31 or 32 bytes accepts them, and so does one with no length check, one that admits 31 bytes or more (off by one), or one that pads a short key to 32 bytes.

raw_reject_vectors.name: raw_key_24_bytes
raw_reject_vectors.note: Raw key bytes: the accept row's first 24 bytes. A raw-bytes entry point that admits AES-192 and AES-256 key sizes (24 or 32 bytes), with or without 16, accepts them.

raw_reject_vectors.name: raw_key_16_bytes
raw_reject_vectors.note: Raw key bytes: the accept row's first 16 bytes. A raw-bytes entry point that admits AES-128 and AES-256 key sizes (16 or 32 bytes) accepts them while refusing 24.

raw_reject_vectors.name: raw_key_33_bytes
raw_reject_vectors.note: Raw key bytes: the accept row's 32 bytes and a 20 byte. A raw-bytes entry point that admits 32 bytes or more, as a hex entry point may, accepts them.

raw_reject_vectors.name: raw_key_ascii_hex_string
raw_reject_vectors.note: Raw key bytes: the 64 ASCII bytes of the accept row's hex string. A raw-bytes entry point that admits 32 bytes or more accepts them and derives a key other than the accept row's; one that hex-decodes 64 hex digits first accepts them as the accept row's key. Both break the rule that a raw-bytes entry point takes exactly 32 bytes.
